subject: Discovery recap + proposed PoC milestones — Ellum Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@ellumhealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed PoC milestones — Ellum Health

Hi Caroline / Tom —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have the same scope for a short PoC: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: inconsistent latency on current NER and summarization endpoints; high token spend from redundant prefix generation; blackbox vendor limits on region/failover.
- Goal: 90th percentile inference latency < 250ms for average 512-token requests, reduce per-session token cost by ~25% through caching/batching, and ensure data residency in us-east for PHI-adjacent flows.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Backend: Python/Flask service on GCP (us-east1)
- Existing LLM vendor: hosted endpoints, no private VPC option, simple REST client
- SDKs used internally: Python (primary), a small Node.js service for realtime webhooks

Success criteria for a minimal PoC
- Latency: 90th < 250ms under a small load (10 rps)
- Cost: 15–30% lower per message token cost compared to current vendor for the same prompts
- Compatibility: seamless Python SDK integration and REST API parity for our routing needs
- Compliance: Redwood can provide SOC 2 artifacts and support an inventory of audit logs during the PoC

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (6 weeks total)
- Week 0 (prep): NDA in place, basic paperwork, exchange of SOC 2 checklist items
- Week 1: Environment setup — onboarding to Redwood Hosted trial with a dedicated project, Python SDK integration sample, smoke tests
- Weeks 2–3: Performance tuning — enable prefix caching, try continuous batching config, collect traces
- Week 4: Load test & compare latency/cost vs current vendor; collect token-level billing breakdown
- Week 5: Integration review & security questionnaire walkthrough
- Week 6: Executive demo + decision review (go/no-go for Dedicated or Private deployment)

Owners / proposed points-of-contact
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Sales/Technical lead), Rafael Mendes (Solutions Engineer)
- Ellum: Caroline Hayes (CTO), Tom Perez (Backend lead)

Next steps I need from you
1) Confirm the PoC owners and preferred PoC start week (we penciled the week of Aug 17).
2) Share your SOC2 checklist (you mentioned a shortened list today) — you can attach it or drop in the Drive link.
3) Confirm whether we should demonstrate Hosted vs Dedicated in the PoC (we can do both but we should agree on one primary config).

Attaching a short MVP PoC plan (redwood-poc-mvp-plan.pdf) that maps tasks to owners and timelines.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the confirmation on owners and start week and will schedule the kickoff call once we have dates.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@ellumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Perez <tom.perez@ellumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed PoC milestones — Ellum Health

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures the convo. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Success criteria: please add a small qualitative metric for answer quality on the NER summaries — our clinical reviewers will score on a 0–5 fidelity scale; we’ll aim for average >= 4.0.
2) SDKs: Python is primary, but our backend team would prefer a Go client if you have it or a short guide on calling the REST API from Go.
3) Data residency: we need confirmation that logs/audit can be restricted to us-east and that Redwood can disable any cross-region replication during the PoC.

I attached our SOC2 items (ellum-soc2-questions.xlsx). We’re comfortable with the week of Aug 17 kickoff assuming NDAs are done — I’ll have legal confirm by EOD Tue.

Also: can you include a rough estimate of the incremental cost if we run the PoC on a small Dedicated pool vs Hosted API? We want to make sure procurement has the right ask.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Hayes
CTO | Ellum Health
caroline.hayes@ellumhealth.com | +1 (917) 222-3344
[Attachment: ellum-soc2-questions.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline.hayes@ellumhealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Tom Perez <tom.perez@ellumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed PoC milestones — Ellum Health

Hi Caroline — great notes, and thanks for the SOC2 file. Quick replies inline and a concrete PoC ask below.

- Quality metric: noted — we’ll build a small eval harness to capture the clinician scores and report average fidelity. Rafael will own the eval script.
- Go support: we don’t have a first-party Go SDK yet, but we have a community-maintained Go client and a short guide for calling the REST endpoints; Rafael will deliver a 1-page "Go quickstart" before kickoff. For tight timelines we can pair-program the initial integration.
- Data residency & logs: we can restrict log exports and disable cross-region replication for your project during the PoC; I’ll include the exact config in the kickoff agenda.
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta: very rough estimate for a 6-week small Dedicated pool (2 gpus reserved): $8k–$12k + usage vs Hosted trial estimated $2k–$3k for equivalent traffic. I’ll get a formal quote from finance before the kickoff.

Concrete asks for the kickoff and timing
1) Confirm Aug 17 as a kickoff date (or propose alternates Aug 24 / Aug 31).
2) Caroline: legal confirmation of NDA and any required PO route.
3) Tom: grant Rafael and me short-term read access to a representative prompt set and a small sample of non-PHI logs so we can run baseline latency tests.

I attached the PoC plan again (redwood-poc-mvp-plan.pdf) and added owners/timeline. If Aug 17 works I’ll send the calendar invite and an agenda with tasks and links to the Drive folder.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
